result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get neighbors of a node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4989-L5091){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.neighbors(node, mode="out") ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the neighboring nodes of a specified node, with control over directionality (for directed graphs). For directed graphs, the default mode is `"out"` (outgoing neighbors only). For undirected graphs, mode doesn't affect the result since all edges are bidirectional. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node ID or label to find neighbors for. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Direction mode for neighbor lookup: (1) `"out"`, only successors (outgoing edges) which is the default for directed graphs, (2) `"in"`, only predecessors (incoming edges), and (3) `"all"`, both successors and predecessors. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of neighbor node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `mode=` is not one of `"out"`, `"in"`, or `"all"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#877cb133 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Directed graph example graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node("A") graph.add_node("B") graph.add_node("C") graph.add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.0) graph.add_edge("C", "A", weight=2.0) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") # Get successors (outgoing neighbors); returns node IDs out_neighbors = graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="out") # Returns []: node IDs, not labels out_neighbors ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [2] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#95fa37e3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Get predecessors (incoming neighbors) in_neighbors = graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="in") # Returns [] in_neighbors ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [3] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#5273f5a4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Get all neighbors all_neighbors = graph.neighbors(a_id, mode="all") # Returns [, ] all_neighbors ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [2, 3] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#b8ebb8e7 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Convert IDs to labels if needed neighbor_labels = [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in out_neighbors] # Returns ['B'] neighbor_labels ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: :::
